senses.def: a large Australian animal that moves by jumping and carries its baby in a pouch
ex: We saw a kangaroo with a baby in its pouch.

senses.def: entertainment in which people sing songs along with recorded music
ex: We sang at a karaoke bar last night.
Do you like karaoke?

senses.def: very interested or eager
ex: He is a keen footballer.
She is keen to learn.

senses.def: very sharp or strong
ex: Dogs have a keen sense of smell.

mistake.note: Use 'keen on' + noun/-ing, or 'keen to' + verb.

senses.def: to continue to have something and not give it away
ex: You can keep the book.
I keep my keys in my bag.

senses.def: to continue doing something, or to stay in a state
ex: Keep calm.
He keeps asking me questions.

senses.def: to do what you promised
ex: She always keeps her promises.

mistake.wrong: He keeps to ask me questions.

senses.def: a person whose job is to look after a place or animals
ex: The zoo keeper feeds the lions.
He is the keeper of the lighthouse.

senses.def: a goalkeeper
ex: The keeper saved the shot.

senses.def: a container with a lid and handle used to boil water
ex: Put the kettle on and make some tea.
The kettle boiled quickly.

senses.def: the set of keys used for typing on a computer
ex: My keyboard has a broken key.
She typed quickly on the keyboard.

senses.def: the set of keys on a piano or similar instrument
ex: He plays the keyboard in a band.

senses.def: a child (informal)
ex: The kids are playing outside.
I have two kids.

senses.def: to say something that is not true as a joke
ex: I'm only kidding.
You're kidding me!

senses.def: to make a person, animal or plant die
ex: The storm killed ten people.
Smoking can kill you.

senses.def: a person or thing that kills
ex: The police are looking for the killer.
Heart disease is a major killer.

senses.def: the act of killing someone
ex: The killing shocked the town.
There have been several killings this year.

senses.def: a type or sort of person or thing
ex: What kind of music do you like?
This is a kind of fruit.

senses.def: friendly, generous and thoughtful towards others
ex: She is a kind woman.
It was kind of you to help.

mistake.wrong: What kinds of food is this?
mistake.right: What kind of food is this?
mistake.note: After 'kind of' and 'sort of', use the singular noun when you ask about one type.

senses.def: the quality of being friendly, generous and caring
ex: Thank you for your kindness.
She treated the animals with kindness.

senses.def: relating to or produced by movement
ex: A moving ball has kinetic energy.

senses.def: a man who is the head of a country, from a royal family
ex: The king lives in a palace.
The old king died last year.

senses.def: a country ruled by a king or queen
ex: The Kingdom of Jordan is in the Middle East.
The prince ruled the kingdom.

senses.def: one of the main groups into which living things are divided
ex: The animal kingdom is very large.

senses.def: a young cat
ex: The kitten drank some milk.
We have two kittens at home.

senses.def: a natural skill or ability to do something easily
ex: She has a knack for making people laugh.
It takes a while to get the knack of it.

senses.def: to go down on one or both knees
ex: He knelt down to tie his shoes.
She knelt beside the bed.

senses.def: the sound of someone hitting a door to ask to come in
ex: There was a knock at the door.
I heard a loud knock.

senses.def: to hit a door or window with your hand to get attention
ex: Please knock before you come in.
Someone is knocking on the door.

senses.def: to hit something so that it moves or falls
ex: He knocked a glass off the table.

senses.def: a place where string, rope or hair is tied or twisted together
ex: I can't untie this knot.
He tied a knot in the rope.

senses.def: a unit of speed for ships and aircraft
ex: The ship was moving at ten knots.

senses.def: to have information about something in your mind
ex: I know the answer.
Do you know where he lives?

senses.def: to be familiar with a person or place
ex: I know her well.
He knows Paris very well.

mistake.note: Use 'know how to + verb', since 'know to' is not used for abilities.

senses.def: the information and understanding you have in your mind
ex: She has a good knowledge of French.
Knowledge is power.

mistake.wrong: I gained many knowledges at university.
mistake.right: I gained a lot of knowledge at university.
mistake.note: 'Knowledge' is uncountable, so it has no plural form.

senses.def: knowing a lot about a subject
ex: The guide was very knowledgeable about the region.
She is knowledgeable about art.

senses.def: recognised by many people
ex: He is a well-known singer.
It is a known fact.
